title: Segmented stage fission with adaptive backpressure and tenant-aware fairness
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: Goal: introduce a segmented stage-fission admission and ordering policy that reduces P95 latency tail without significantly sacrificing aggregate throughput, while preserving tenant-level fairness.
description_continued: Motivation: current monolithic stage processing causes long-tail latencies when large prefill requests collide with long decode streams. We will split requests at scheduling time into short segments using a lightweight cost estimator (attention cost + kernel latency hint + token budget), then interleave segments across prefill and decode pipelines with an adaptive backpressure controller.
success_criteria: 1) P95 end-to-end latency reduction >= 8% on mixed workload benchmarks; 2) throughput degradation <= 6% at steady state; 3) fairness index (Jain) neutral or improved across tenants; 4) no QoS regressions for Dedicated customers.
deliverables: Design doc with segment heuristics and backpressure formulas
Prototype scheduler and admission controller in staging
Canary runbook and console telemetry dashboard
decision_points: Segment boundary: fixed-token windows vs attention-cost quantiles
Fairness accounting: proportional token credits vs strict round-robin
Backpressure: multiplicative drop vs admission delay
tradeoffs: Smaller segments improve latency interleaving but increase scheduler overhead and kernel context switches
Stricter fairness protects tenants but can reduce global throughput
Kernel churn can increase if segments frequently change kernel affinity
kernel_integration_notes: Scheduler will consult kernel-hint API to prefer low-latency attention kernels for short decode segments and avoid splitting when kernel switch cost is high. Coalescing heuristic will merge adjacent segments that map to same kernel to reduce context switches.
compatibility: Works with existing prefix/KV cache and hedging. Must ensure segment metadata is safe to pass through KV cache and not leak prompts in telemetry.
rollout_plan: Simulation -> staging canary (dev-region) -> 10% tenant canary with telemetry -> gradual ramp with rollback gates.
